summary: Iteration 2 testing for file uploads, audit logs and reimbursement status. Backend: 14/14 pytest tests passed (test_iteration2.py) covering POST/GET/DELETE /api/files with mime+size validation and Bearer/query-param auth, audit logs for transactions/projects/dividends/reimbursements (create/update/delete), reimbursement_status transitions pending->reimbursed via source_transaction_ids and null for income/non-personal, file_id round-trip on transactions, audit endpoint sorting+filters+auth. Frontend: Auditoría nav link visible & routes to /audit. AuditLog page renders 21 audit rows with ACCIÓN badges (CREÓ/EDITÓ/ELIMINÓ), partner avatars, timestamps and 'hace Xs' relative time; filter by action=create correctly reduced to 11 rows. Transactions page renders 'Estado' and 'Archivo' columns, 'Nuevo movimiento' modal contains FileUploader (data-testid='file-uploader', 'file-pick') with COMPROBANTE label, and rows display inline 'por [Partner]' AuditBadge. End-to-end UI submission of personal expense + reimbursement creation could not be visually verified due to a description textarea selector mismatch in the test (the modal validation 'Please fill out this field' fired), but backend e2e equivalent passed.

minor.issue: Token passed as ?auth= query param appears in server access logs (security trade-off vs <a href>). Consider short-lived signed URLs in future.
MAX_FILE_SIZE check happens AFTER reading the entire body into memory (await file.read()). A 100MB upload still consumes RAM before being rejected. Use streaming or Content-Length pre-check.

PUT replaces all fields and re-stamps created_* only via stamp_update; if the PUT payload omits an optional field it overwrites with default (e.g. file_id becomes null if not sent). Use PATCH or include $set with payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True).
No PUT endpoint exposed (only POST/GET/DELETE) - intentional? source_transaction_ids cannot be edited after creation; user must delete + recreate.
Soft-delete only flips is_deleted in DB; the underlying object in Emergent storage is never removed. Acceptable for audit/restore but should be documented.

integration_issues.issue: Modal overlay (fixed inset-0 z-50) intercepts pointer events on the sidebar; after opening it from /transactions, navigation links can't be clicked until modal is closed. Esc/Cancelar works, so it's not user-blocking but Playwright force=False clicks fail. Consider listening for nav clicks to auto-close, or just confirm Cancelar is reachable.

action_items: (Minor) Stream-validate upload size or check Content-Length before reading body to avoid loading >10MB into memory.
(Minor) Add PATCH or use exclude_unset on transaction PUT so partial updates don't blank out file_id / paid_personally / project_id.
(Minor) Decide whether reimbursements need a PUT endpoint to edit linked source_transaction_ids.
(Polish) Auto-close the Tx modal when sidebar nav is clicked to prevent overlay click-jacking.
(Polish) Document soft-delete behavior of /api/files/{id} (object remains in storage).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 742 lines mixing models, routes, storage, auth, seed and audit helpers. Strongly recommend splitting into /backend/routers (files, transactions, audit, ...), /backend/models, /backend/storage.py and /backend/auth.py before next iteration.

init_storage() is sync and called inside async request handlers via put_object/get_object using `requests` (blocking). Under load this will block the FastAPI event loop. Switch to httpx.AsyncClient or run via asyncio.to_thread.

_decorate_txs loads ALL reimbursements (to_list(2000)) on every /api/transactions list call - O(N*M). For larger datasets, build the linked-id set once via aggregation or store reimbursement_status denormalized on the tx and update it transactionally.

stamp_update mutates the payload dict in place AND only adds updated_* keys; created_by_id/created_by_name are preserved only because the $set update doesn't include them, but if model_dump ever emitted them they'd be overwritten. Consider exclude={'created_*'} on update payloads.

log_audit is awaited but is fire-and-forget logically; if Mongo write fails the API request still succeeds silently (no try/except, but the await will raise). Consider wrapping log_audit calls in try/except so a logging failure doesn't 500 the user-facing operation.
Pydantic models lack PositiveFloat / max-length / future-date guards on amount, description, date. Easy hardening.

success_rate.frontend: 5/6 surfaces verified; e2e badge transition verified at backend layer
